description:
Connect a neopixel to your circuit.

Using any combination of buttons, touch sensors, or potentiometers, create a device that allows the user to choose between a selection of colors or any color.

For example: tapping the buttons moves the led through a list of colors or, turning the knob moves the led through the rainbow.

 

1. Post your code here with a description of what it does and how it works.
2. Bring your working circuit into class and show it to me.

 

Adafruit tutorial

Starter Code

The following (untested) code allows the user to choose from 6 colors by turning a knob. Other possibilities are: tap a button to change colors or, led cycles through rainbow and a button can stop and start it.

import time
import board
import neopixel

pixel_pin = board.GP12

RED = (255, 0, 0, 0)
YELLOW = (255, 150, 0, 0)
GREEN = (0, 255, 0, 0)
CYAN = (0, 255, 255, 0)
BLUE = (0, 0, 255, 0)
PURPLE = (180, 0, 255, 0)

set pot_pin to analogin
create pot_value variable

while True:
    pot_value = pot_pin analog in
    if pot_value < 10922:    #this 65535 / the number of colors
        pixels.fill(RED)
    else if pot_value >= 10922 AND pot.value < 21844:
        pixels.fill(YELLOW)
    else if  #keep going for other colors
    pixels.show()
    time.sleep(.05)

description:
Follow the Adafruit instructions to set up your microcontroller development environment.

In brief:

1. Download the circuitpython UTF file.

2. Plug in the pico to USB while holding the button down.

3. Drag the UTF file onto the device which appears on your computer.

4. The pico will restart with a file called code.py. The code you write to this file will run on the pico.

(The instructions go on to describe blinking the onboard LED. This will not work and you will skip ahead to using a real LED on your breadboard)
name: Raspberry Pi Pico Development Environment

description:
It is go time. We need to make progress every week on our object. We need to start building as soon as possible.

In order to do that, we must certain information.

A typical object will require: An enclosure with a place to mount the electronics and a place to mount the controls.

Your object does not need to look like what you want the final product to look like. You may create a working prototype in a simple box along with the visual designs of what the completed project would look.

In order to build our object, you must know which parts you will use and what size they are.

This will allow you to create a:

  • BOM (bill of materials) with links to the parts, measurements, and links to any tutorials.
  • Mechanical Drawing with measurements.
  • Circuit diagram
  • Prototype circuit on solderless breadboard
  • List of questions / concerns to ask me (a written list of questions counts towards completion of this assignment.)

It is likely that you will not have all the knowledge you need and that is what the questions are for.

This assignment has no specific requirements and is based on the progress you present in class.
name: Emergent Object: PROGRESS REPORT 1

description:
Have most of your parts on your solderless breadboard. Most of the wiring is pretty simple.

Capacitive touch sensor or just like buttons.

The SSD1306 only has 4 wires to connect.

Neopixels only need a single resistor to chain together any number of LEDs.

The realTimeClock is great. You can do a lot with a device that can tell time and date. It has only 4 wires.

The HC-SR04 range finder has two connections besides power/ground and requires a 10k resistor to ground.

Connect a speaker between a pin and ground and you can make noise. audio.md piano.md
name: Prototype Circuit
